BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE HIRDESH  ON THE 6 th OF JANUARY, 2026  MISC. APPEAL No. 1657 of 2009  NEW INDIA ASSURANCE CO.LTD.
 Versus
RAJESH KUMAR BOHARE AND OTHERS

Appearance:
 Shri Arvind Agarwal - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri S.D. Singh - Advocate for the respondents.

ORDER This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant-Insurance Company assailing the award dated 30.09.2009 passed by the Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhind (M.P.) in Claim Case No.23/2008, whereby the learned Claims Tribunal directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount to the claimant with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 27-12-2006, after completing his studies at Jain College,
claimant along with Netram, was returning to his village on a motorcycle bearing registration No.
MP-30-BA-2068, which was being driven by Bunty.

entities.text: Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhind (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: When they reached near Phuap Mandi, a Maruti car bearing registration No. MP-30-C-0519, owned and driven by Megh Singh, came at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the motorcycle.
As a result of the said accident, the claimant sustained NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:306 2 MA-1657-2009 injuries.

A report was lodged at the concerned police station and, after investigation,
the challan was filed before the competent Court.
Thereafter, a claim petition was filed before the Claims Tribunal, which resulted in passing of the impugned award.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the impugned award is contrary to law and facts New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Rajesh Kumar Bohare on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20035449/
1 and hence unsustainable.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Rajesh Kumar Bohare
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is contended that the learned Claims Tribunal has recorded a clear finding that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence on the date of the accident i.e. 27-12-2006, amounting to breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

It is further submitted that despite such finding, the learned Tribunal has wrongly fastened initial liability upon the Insurance Company and granted recovery rights against the owner,
which according to the appellant is impermissible in law where there is a clear violation of policy conditions.
It is also submitted that possession of a valid driving licence is a condition precedent for fastening liability upon the Insurance Company, which admittedly was not fulfilled in the present case.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents opposed the appeal and supported the impugned award.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record of the Claims Tribunal.
6.

On perusal of the impugned award, it is found that it is undisputed that at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence,
which constitutes a breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
7. However, it is also undisputed that the claimant is a third party.

In NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:306 3 MA-1657-2009 such circumstances, the settled position of law is that the Insurance Company cannot avoid its statutory liability towards a third-party claimant.
The learned Claims Tribunal has rightly directed the Insurance Company to satisfy the award in the first instance with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

8. This Court finds that the learned Claims Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record and has correctly applied the principle of "pay and recover" to balance the rights of the third-party claimant and the Insurance Company.
No illegality or perversity is found in the impugned award warranting interference by this Court.
9. Accordingly, the miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellant- Insurance Company is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
